headline: Congress condemns the August 2017 Charlottesville violence, honors the first responders who died, and urges the President to act against hate groups.
what_it_does: This joint resolution formally condemns the violent attack in Charlottesville, Virginia, during events on August 11 and 12, 2017. It recognizes the first responders who died while monitoring the events and offers condolences to the families of those killed and support to those injured. It also rejects white nationalists, white supremacists, the Ku Klux Klan, neo-Nazis, and other hate groups, and urges the President and Cabinet to use available resources against them. It does not create new rules, funding, or programs.
when_it_takes_effect: It took effect when it was enacted on September 14, 2017.
